business_description: HP Inc. is a global technology company operating in more than 170 countries. It sells personal-computing devices, printers, supplies, software, services and subscriptions, including AI PCs and workstations, endpoint-security solutions, hybrid-work systems, gaming products, commercial and consumer printing, graphics printing and 3D-printing solutions. Personal Systems serves enterprises, public-sector organizations, small and medium businesses and consumers; Printing serves home users, small and medium businesses, public-sector and large-enterprise customers, print-service providers, packaging converters and digital-manufacturing customers. FY2025 net revenue was $55,295 million: Personal Systems $38,532 million, or about 69.7% of total; Printing $16,702 million, or about 30.2%; Corporate Investments $62 million, or about 0.1%. Within Personal Systems, Commercial PS contributed $27,438 million and Consumer PS $11,094 million. Within Printing, Supplies contributed $10,916 million, Commercial Printing $4,633 million and Consumer Printing $1,153 million. FY2025 geographic revenue was Americas $23,545 million, Europe/Middle East/Africa $18,596 million and Asia-Pacific/Japan $13,154 million. Products represented $52,002 million, or 94.0% of FY2025 revenue, while Services represented $3,293 million, or 6.0%. Pricing-power evidence is mixed: FY2025 consolidated gross margin declined from 22.1% to 20.6% because higher commodity and tariff costs, adverse mix and currency more than offset disciplined pricing and cost savings. In Q3 FY2026, Personal Systems ASPs rose 40.8%, primarily from price actions, currency and mix, but PC unit volume fell 15.8% and segment operating margin declined from 5.4% to 4.6%, so the filings do not demonstrate that HP could raise prices without volume loss. Printing showed better resilience: Q3 FY2026 Printing operating margin rose from 17.0% to 18.1%, with pricing actions and tariff refunds contributing, although segment revenue declined 2.2%.
moat_evidence: Intangible Assets: HP reported a worldwide portfolio of more than 16,000 patents as of October 31, 2025 and states that it seeks patent protection where proprietary rights can maintain or improve its competitive position. HP also states that no single patent is essential to the business.

Intangible Assets / Brand and product ecosystem: HP identifies its brand, R&D and security capabilities, broad product portfolio, ability to cross-sell, service and support offerings, product accessibility and broad distribution as competitive advantages in Personal Systems; for Printing it similarly cites brand, innovation, security capabilities, breadth of solutions and distribution.

Low-Cost Production / operating scale: HP uses outsourced manufacturers globally to generate cost efficiencies, shorten time to market and preserve supply-chain flexibility. It also states that build-to-order manufacturing maximizes manufacturing and logistics efficiency through high-volume base configurations. The filings do not provide peer manufacturing-cost comparisons proving a structural lowest-cost position.

growth_driver_evidence.sales_marketing: Not disclosed in the provided filings
growth_driver_evidence.distribution_channels: HP states that the majority of overall revenue is generated through channel resellers, supplemented by direct online sales, retailers, commercial resellers, distributors and systems integrators. It also describes the reseller landscape as having increasing online and omnichannel presence. The filings describe broad existing routes to market rather than a separately quantified newly launched channel.
growth_driver_evidence.geographic_expansion: A specific new-country expansion is not disclosed. Adjacent-market expansion is disclosed: HP's Printing strategy includes expanding its 3D-printing footprint across digital manufacturing and strategic applications, while Personal Systems targets endpoint services, Device-as-a-Service and hybrid-system adjacencies.
growth_driver_evidence.acquisitions: Not disclosed in the provided filings
growth_driver_evidence.pricing_power: HP has demonstrated an ability to take pricing actions, but the filings do not establish an ability to raise prices without losing customers or units. In Q3 FY2026 Personal Systems ASPs rose 40.8% primarily from pricing actions, currency and mix, while PC units fell 15.8%; for the first nine months, ASPs rose 19.8% while units fell 4.2%. HP explicitly states that the higher-cost environment resulted in both higher ASPs and lower PC units. Personal Systems operating margin nevertheless declined to 4.6% from 5.4% in Q3 and to 4.9% from 5.2% for the first nine months. In Printing, Q3 hardware ASPs increased 5.8% while printer units fell 6.8%; pricing actions helped raise Printing operating margin to 18.1% from 17.0%, but Supplies revenue fell 2.8% as installed base and usage declined.
growth_driver_evidence.new_products: HP identifies a new line of AI PCs and workstations capable of local AI processing and intelligent-print features incorporated into home, office and graphics offerings. It is also emphasizing subscription-oriented Printing offerings such as Instant Ink, HP All-In Plan and Managed Print Services.
growth_driver_evidence.customer_retention: The filings do not provide a customer-retention, renewal or churn percentage. They do show recurring behavior and contractual revenue alongside customer optionality: Printing supplies are consumables intended for recurring use in installed hardware, while standard services agreements are generally renewable at the customer's option and may permit early termination. HP reported $4.3 billion of remaining performance obligations at October 31, 2025, of which approximately $1.9 billion was expected within the following 12 months, but this is contracted backlog rather than a retention rate.

risk_evidence.concentration: Customer concentration increased above HP's 10% disclosure threshold in FY2025: TD SYNNEX Corp represented 12% of HP net revenue, whereas no single customer represented 10% or more in FY2024 or FY2023.
risk_evidence.disruption: HP states that rapid innovation and technological change can render its products uneconomical or obsolete and cause market-share loss if it cannot keep pace. HP also says AI may significantly affect customer preferences and market dynamics, that unsuccessful AI products could fail to recoup investment or damage competitiveness, and that AI products could cannibalize traditional non-AI products. Conversely, HP already sells AI PCs and workstations and is incorporating intelligent features into Printing. HP also disclosed that the Windows-based PC operating-system refresh supported Personal Systems demand in FY2026.
risk_evidence.outside_forces: HP is exposed to tariffs, commodity and component inflation, supply constraints, foreign exchange and interest rates. HP stated that substantial new U.S. import tariffs began in April 2025 and that FY2025 commodity and tariff costs were not fully mitigated by pricing and other actions. It specifically identified memory and storage inflation and potential Personal Systems supply constraints. In FY2026, HP continued to cite increasing memory and storage costs and uncertainty about the market's ability to absorb price increases. Mitigation includes supply-chain resiliency actions, cost measures and pricing. HP also hedges foreign-exchange and interest-rate exposures using derivatives, including forward contracts and, at times, options.
risk_evidence.competition: HP describes both Personal Systems and Printing as highly competitive. Named Personal Systems competitors include Acer, Apple, ASUS, Dell, Huawei, Lenovo, Logitech, Microsoft, Samsung and Toshiba. Named Printing competitors include Brother, Canon, Pantum, Epson, Ricoh and Xerox. Printing also competes with lower-priced non-original, refill and remanufactured supplies. HP reported demand softness and competitive pressures in Printing in FY2026, with nine-month printer unit volume down 6.6%. The filings do not disclose comparable operating margins for named peers, so no filing-supported peer-margin advantage can be asserted.

price_sentiment_narrative: HP's filings provide a historical one-year shareholder-return narrative through October 31, 2025 rather than a current September 2026 market-price assessment. HP's cumulative-total-return index, including reinvested dividends, declined from 224.51 at October 2024 to 182.07 at October 2025, implying approximately -18.9% total shareholder return. Over the same interval, the filing's S&P 500 index rose from 185.38 to 225.10, about +21.4%, and the S&P Information Technology Index rose from 231.83 to 318.88, about +37.5%, so HP materially underperformed both filing-selected benchmarks. Analyst/institutional sentiment is not disclosed in the provided filings. Filing-supported bull arguments include nine-month FY2026 revenue growth of 9.5%, Personal Systems revenue growth of 14.4%, support from the Windows PC refresh, pricing actions offsetting part of higher commodity costs, and Printing maintaining an 18.2% nine-month operating margin despite declining revenue. HP's Fiscal 2026 Plan also targets productivity through AI adoption and simplification, including a planned global headcount reduction of approximately 4,000 to 6,000 through FY2028. Filing-supported bear arguments include nine-month FY2026 gross margin declining to 19.8% from 20.7%, net earnings falling to $1,656 million from $1,734 million, Personal Systems margin compression despite large ASP increases, and continued Printing pressure from declining installed base, lower usage, weaker printer units and competition. FY2025 had already shown consolidated gross margin declining to 20.6% from 22.1% and net earnings falling to $2,529 million from $2,775 million.

ai_risk_evidence.liability: HP explicitly states that AI development and use create competitive, reputational and liability risks. It also warns that accelerated innovation in supplier components can create defects or performance failures that could increase warranty costs, inventory provisions or impairments and reduce future sales. The filings do not quantify the financial cost of an individual AI error and do not state that human oversight is indispensable or cannot be replaced by AI.
ai_risk_evidence.business_model: Current reported revenue is predominantly product-based rather than disclosed as per-user or seat-based. For the nine months ended July 31, 2026, Products generated $41,986 million, or 94.3% of revenue, and Services $2,537 million, or 5.7%. HP's Products category includes hardware, supplies, subscriptions and software licenses, so the filing does not permit a clean split between unit-based hardware and supplies versus seat-based or subscription software. The evidence therefore supports describing HP as primarily exposed to physical product and unit economics, while the precise seat-based revenue share is not disclosed.
ai_risk_evidence.physical_world: The core business materially depends on the physical world. Personal Systems sells desktops, notebooks, workstations, displays, point-of-sale systems and hybrid systems; Printing sells printers and recurring physical supplies. HP uses outsourced manufacturers worldwide to produce HP-designed products and also assembles finished products from purchased components and subassemblies. AI therefore cannot eliminate the need for hardware production, component procurement, logistics and physical-device fulfillment represented by the current reported revenue mix.
ai_risk_evidence.network: Not disclosed in the provided filings

bear.assumption: Analyst judgment for FY2031, treated as FY+5 from FY2026. PAT is modeled using GAAP net earnings as the PAT-equivalent in the pipeline's Yahoo Finance fallback unit of USD millions. Bear PAT of approximately $2,000 million assumes continued Printing installed-base and usage decline, persistent PC commodity and tariff pressure, price and mix increases temporarily lifting revenue while falling unit volumes erode the installed base and future replacement demand (Q3 FY2026 Personal Systems revenue +18% on units -16%), and Fiscal 2026 Plan productivity benefits failing to offset margin pressure. The downside case is grounded in nine-month FY2026 Personal Systems operating margin declining to 4.9% from 5.2%, Printing revenue declining 1.5%, and consolidated gross margin declining to 19.8% from 20.7%.

base.assumption: Analyst judgment for FY2031, treated as FY+5 from FY2026. Base PAT of approximately $3,000 million assumes Personal Systems growth normalizes after the current pricing and Windows-refresh cycle; Printing revenue remains structurally challenged but operating margin remains broadly in the high teens; and the Fiscal 2026 Plan's AI-enabled productivity, simplification and planned 4,000 to 6,000 headcount reduction provide enough cost benefit by FY2028 to recover part of recent margin compression. FY2025 net earnings of $2,529 million and nine-month FY2026 net earnings of $1,656 million are the historical anchors. The filings describe outsourced manufacturing rather than a material owned-capacity expansion, so no capacity-build uplift is assumed.

bull.assumption: Analyst judgment for FY2031, treated as FY+5 from FY2026. Bull PAT of approximately $4,000 million assumes AI PCs, workstations and premium mix sustain Personal Systems growth; HP retains enough pricing to offset commodity inflation while segment margins recover; endpoint services, subscriptions and hybrid-system adjacencies grow; 3D and digital-printing expansion contributes incremental growth; Printing operating margin remains near its recent high-teens level; and the Fiscal 2026 Plan produces durable productivity improvement through FY2028. FY2026 GAAP EPS guidance of $2.52-$2.62 (~$2.4B at ~920M weighted shares) includes $0.19 of one-time tariff refunds, so underlying FY2026 PAT is closer to ~$2.2B; $4B is an implied CAGR of ~11% from reported guidance or ~13% from underlying. Hurdles for the 12x multiple: Personal Systems operating margin sustainably 6%+, Printing operating margin 17-19%, Printing/Supplies decline slowing substantially, services/subscription earnings becoming a meaningful share, FCF consistently ~$4B+, continued share-count reduction; without this quality improvement a 9-10x multiple is more appropriate.
